# Case Study: Peak Season & Getcho Delivery: Taking the Heat Off Store Teams | Getcho

**URL:** [https://getcho.app/success-story/handling-same-day-local-delivery-peak-season/](https://getcho.app/success-story/handling-same-day-local-delivery-peak-season/)

Those working in retail know peak season as December, Black Friday, and Cyber Monday. For Eataly , it sure is. But specialty retailers might qualify that:

- Halloween is peak, says Abracadabra , one of the top costume retailers

- In grocery, peak might be the week of Thanksgiving or the day before the Super Bowl

- Myers Keswick in New York City has all hands on deck for Easter

- Valentine’s day is a rush for Funny Face Bakery ; people love to gift their cookies!

- When the Bears play is as busy as it gets for Clark Street Sports

- Brands like Flaus pop off after founder appearances on Good Morning America

- When the weather man is wrong and it doesn’t snow, PR Running knows to be ready

While the busy season might vary, the objective does not: capture the volume while not being overrun. Getcho helps brands and retailers do just that.

## The Challenge

Fail to prepare for the rush and you might fail to capture potential sales while hurting the brand (“the line was so long!”). Chaos breeds employee turnover. It certainly messes with inventory precision.

## The Solution

Getcho partners know us as a reliable release valve for busy times. Whether it’s making in-store pickups more regular and controllable, using dynamic price controls to modulate same day delivery, or giving ops more time to prep orders – don’t worry about the UPS cut-off today, Getcho can send a courier tomorrow and still get it there quicker – Getcho will take the heat off.

## Abracadabra

Abracadabra is New York City’s top Halloween dealer. Prior to working with Getcho, they enforced a mail cut-off date a few days before October 31st. Because when the post office delivers on November 1st, you can bet the customer will be asking for a refund. They no longer have to sacrifice their eCommerce volume on the 30th and 31st!

They also get insane foot traffic. So they were delighted that Getcho could coordinate batched pick-ups only when they had marked orders as ready. We all know about the BOPIS customers who show up before the order is picked…

Getcho empowers Abracadabra to set dynamic delivery pricing rules. Under strain, it’s more work to pack a delivery, so it makes sense to charge more.

Finally, Abracadabra gets heavy use of our “Send to Getcho” feature. This lets them move a mail order to courier delivery, effectively buying them two more days to pack an order.

## Eataly

Eataly’s tidal wave comes during the holiday as customers and companies send bottles and bottles of wine as gifts.

Eataly Vino customers are empowered to schedule their deliveries at their convenience, thereby eliminating returns. That’s one less thing for the store to worry about.

Getcho also helped Eataly batch large holiday food orders, reducing the pickup footprint from dozens to just one. For the more irregular courier deliveries, Getcho allowed Eataly to change the pick-up location to a dedicated counter; Getcho used pick-up photos to make sure drivers grabbed the right thing.

>

You’re amazing!! Thank you so much for helping me to make Christmas special for my husband!!

— Eataly Vino customer

>

My delivery was very smooth and it came much earlier than I expected. Just a note that this is an excellent wine. I’ll take time writing a review tonight. Thank you again for the fantastic service.

— Eataly Vino customer

## Ninja Transfers

Ninja Transfers is America’s top DTF company. Many of their customers are other businesses who use Ninja DTFs to produce custom apparel which they sell to end-consumers.

Getcho takes the heat off of Ninja Transfers business customers who have busy seasons of their own. The soccer uniform companies can buy themselves an extra few days as the Fall rolls around – maybe your 8 year old will appreciate that their jersey was rushed from business to business before being handed out at practice.

>

The brand was blown away by the speed of this! They had 600+ garments arrive with no printing and needed to get it to the print shop ASAP to make Christmas. Huge win for them!

— Ninja Transfers

---

Retailers use Getcho to handle local and same day delivery during their busiest periods, so store and operations teams can stay focused on customers, not logistics.

## Key Takeaways

- Peak season varies by vertical : Halloween for costume retailers, holidays for wine shops, Valentine’s Day for bakeries, game days for sports retailers. Getcho scales to all of them.

- Abracadabra (NYC costume retailer) eliminated their pre-Halloween mail cutoff date, uses dynamic delivery pricing during surges, and coordinates batched pickups so drivers only arrive when orders are ready.

- Eataly Vino lets customers schedule wine deliveries at their convenience (eliminating returns), batches large holiday food orders into single pickups, and uses pickup photos to verify correct packages.

- Ninja Transfers (America’s top DTF company) uses Getcho to rush-deliver custom apparel between businesses, buying their B2B customers extra days during peak seasons.

- Getcho’s “Send to Getcho” feature lets retailers convert a mail order to courier delivery on the fly, buying 2+ extra days to pack an order during crunch time.

For most stores we also recommend barcode verification at pickup, which scans each item against the order so the wrong package is caught before it ever leaves the door. And when it's a no-harm mix-up (a driver marks picked up without actually grabbing the order, or returns unnecessarily), Getcho will often redispatch on the store's behalf automatically — frequently before anyone has to lift a finger. We stay very hands-on with our store teams.

### What happens after I send an order to Getcho via API, and how fast is it assigned to a driver?

For all intents and purposes, immediately. Once a quote is accepted, the order enters dispatch. Our most common workflow assigns the cheapest available carrier, and in that case the order is assigned to a delivery partner right away. If speed is what you care about most, we can optimize for the fastest available driver instead — dispatch is modular, so we're happy to chat about what fits your operation. For orders scheduled in advance, the same applies as the delivery window approaches, and scheduled orders can be canceled for free up until dispatch.

### Can I update an order after it has been sent to Getcho but before a driver is assigned?

Yes — this happens all the time, and we use APIs to update orders on the fly. Before a driver is assigned, order details can be modified directly. Even after a driver has picked up, reach out and we can usually still get updated instructions where they need to go.

### If a driver is already assigned and I need to cancel because the order isn't ready, how does that work — and who covers the cost?

It depends on timing. If a driver is already en route, the fleet usually charges a cancellation fee, which is passed along. If the cancellation was due to a Getcho dispatch mistake, Getcho may absorb that fee. And if "not ready yet" is something your store runs into regularly, let's talk — we've got solutions, including dispatching only once an order is actually packed rather than purely around the scheduled window.

# Case Study: Home Field Advantage: Capturing New Local Delivery Markets | Getcho

**URL:** [https://getcho.app/success-story/home-field-advantage-local-delivery-markets/](https://getcho.app/success-story/home-field-advantage-local-delivery-markets/)

>

Good morning! I honestly can’t thank you enough. Delivery was amazing and shirts are all done and ready to be worn at nationals!

— Ninja Transfers customer

Proximity is an advantage. eCommerce brands do proportionally more order volume where they have a retail presence.

- City Man USA , for example, does more orders in the Detroit market than their out-of-state competitors

- Getcho partners in the NYC market sometimes do 30-40% of their orders in New York, New York — more than 3x higher than outsider brands

The “homefield effect” usually applies within a small radius of a storefront. Getcho helps partners capture more orders by expanding the radius by orders of magnitude.

## The Challenge

The median BOPIS customer lives within 3 miles of the pick-up location. Even in the densest areas, it’s hard to position a storefront within 3 miles of that many people. How can a brand reap more from stores and production centers?

Take Ninja Transfers . Their facility sits north of Philadelphia, only 15 minutes away from the New Jersey border. They could already technically boast that BOPIS customers come from out of state.

Even so, a customer probably won’t make a two hour drive from places like New York City, Maryland, or East New Jersey. And in the DTF business, you can’t just sprout up new locations.

## The Solution

Getcho and Ninja Transfers launched a 120-mile same-day delivery range, enveloping New York City, northern Maryland and everything in between.

Launch was shockingly easy; Getcho’s Shopify plugin automatically adds courier delivery for carts within a predefined radius, on a dynamic set of products. It works perfectly on its own, or alongside plugins like Advanced Shipping Rules , custom OMSs, you name it.

After launch, we immediately started seeing daily orders from every corner of the new range. What’s more: these customers retain better – it’s common to see two orders from the same customer within one day. Plus same-day customers have a bigger AOV.

## The Results

- Launching “Northeast Same Day Delivery” required no set-up

- The new shipping rate is comparable to the slower “next-day delivery”

- Customer retention is 2x higher than for standard expedited shipping

- Business customers especially took to using same-day delivery frequently

- Fridays are particularly popular days for Same Day Delivery as customers look to receive orders before the weekend

---

Ninja Transfers uses Getcho to expand reach, meet urgent demand, and increase sales from nearby customers without making delivery something the team has to manage.

## Key Takeaways

- The “homefield effect” : E-commerce brands do disproportionately more order volume near their physical locations. Getcho expands that radius by orders of magnitude.

- Ninja Transfers launched a 120-mile same-day delivery range from their Philadelphia-area facility, covering NYC, northern Maryland, and everything in between — with zero setup.

- Same-day delivery customers retain 2x better than standard expedited shipping customers and have higher average order values.

- Business-to-business customers are especially heavy users of same-day delivery, often placing multiple orders in a single day.

- Getcho’s Shopify plugin automatically shows “same-day delivery” at checkout only for customers within a predefined radius, working alongside existing shipping rules.

Getcho has been extremely helpful in expanding our range of delivery options. And, since we started using Getcho about two months ago, there has been a significant drop in customer experience issues related to third-party delivery. The Getcho team is hands-on and highly responsive to feedback.

— Director of Systems, Farm Link Hawai’i

When to tap your own fleet and when to outsource delivery is both an art and a science. Check out our case study on supplementing in-house drivers . You’d be in good company with Janovic and Farm Link !

## We have an account with a 3rd-party fleet

That’s great. Getcho probably supports your 3rd-party integration. And more importantly, if you depend on a single network, you’re probably leaving money on the table.

Some fleets are great for distance, going 25+ miles on-demand. Other fleets are great at economically handling close deliveries.

Getcho orchestrates, using the best network for the job. We saved Eataly 18% on their local deliveries by offering them a broader network. Farm Link Hawai’i doubled their radius with Getcho, offering delivery where they couldn’t previously.

## We aggregate 3rd-party fleets already

Another step in the right direction. Let me give you one more reason to use Getcho:

Getcho is the only service that owns the delivery. Does that sound like a paradox? It just means we don’t just kick deliveries over to a network and tell you to deal with them. We’re the ones talking with their support team, their drivers, and signing off on every delivery. The tracking page has your logo on it.

## Finding the best rate

Finding the best rate for a delivery isn’t as simple as checking the networks. It involves analyzing meta-reliability:

- What’s Roadie’s average time in transit?

- How many stops does a DoorDash driver typically have?

- Is it worth paying $6 more to guarantee a delivery before 1pm, or does the customer not care?

- That answer probably changes when you’re talking about paint vs. perishables.

---

Getcho helps partners decide when to use their own fleet and when to outsource—maximizing efficiency while keeping customers happy.

## Key Takeaways

- Hybrid fleet strategy is the sweet spot: use your own trucks for planned routes and outsource urgent or out-of-zone deliveries to Getcho’s multi-fleet network.

- Getcho saved Eataly 18% on local deliveries by giving them access to a broader courier network instead of relying on a single carrier.

- Farm Link Hawaii doubled their delivery radius with Getcho, reaching zip codes their own trucks couldn’t serve cost-effectively.

- Getcho owns the delivery — unlike other aggregators that hand off to a network and walk away, Getcho coordinates with drivers, support teams, and signs off on every delivery.

- Rate optimization is multidimensional : the best rate depends on average transit time, driver stop count, time guarantees, and cargo type — not just the sticker price.

<a id="success-story-packiyo-highline-commerce-sameday-delivery"></a>

# Case Study: Highline Commerce + Getcho: Same Day Delivery in New York & Atlanta | Getcho

**URL:** [https://getcho.app/success-story/packiyo-highline-commerce-sameday-delivery/](https://getcho.app/success-story/packiyo-highline-commerce-sameday-delivery/)

## The Results

>

Getcho has solved not only the reliability, but also the visibility into costs, and most importantly a trusted customer experience. They have regularly gone above and beyond to make it easy for our team, quickly incorporated our feedback, and become a critical part of our day-to-day operations: serving some of our biggest customers like Coca-Cola and Delta.

- Richard Hurley - Cofounder and CEO at Highline Commerce

- Trusted by major brands including Coca-Cola and Delta

- 92 minutes average delivery time

- Seamless integration with existing Packiyo WMS workflows

## The Challenge

Highline Commerce is a leading 3rd-party logistics (3PL) company strategically positioned in Brooklyn and Atlanta to provide same-day and next-day delivery to customers. While many 3PLs target cheap leases in rural areas, Highline Commerce places their fulfillment centers close to dense cities to minimize shipping time and costs.

The brands they served were eager to offer their customers immediate courier delivery from the warehouse. But given the many moving parts of a 3PL, arranging seamless, fast courier service from a fulfillment center was disruptive and chaotic.

Over the past five years, using a variety of single same-day carriers, they would regularly see:

- Orders costing more than expected

- Deliveries not arriving on time

- Overall poor customer experience

High-end brands are particularly keen to offer immediate delivery because it enables them to target VIP customers who make more frequent purchases and are willing to pay more for immediate service.

## The Previous Process

Before Getcho, brands attempted to cobble together courier delivery service:

- Generic shipping options - Brands would add a new generic shipping option to checkout and hope only nearby customers would use it

- Manual coordination - As orders arrived, they would email their Highline Commerce contact requesting faster processing

- Disjointed pickup - Brand managers would monitor fulfillment status and try to arrange pickup using a courier. Because couriers were not integrated with Highline’s system, they were often hesitant to pick up or unable to find the correct package

- Lost packages - Because couriers had no way to provide proof of delivery photos, no support line, packages were lost

- Poor customer experience - Even successful deliveries lacked shipping progress notifications or branded tracking, leading to a sub-par brand experience

## The Solution

Getcho partnered with Highline Commerce to help brands offer same-day delivery directly from their Shopify sites by simply installing the Getcho app .

Getcho built an integration with Highline’s warehouse-management-software (WMS), Packiyo . Now, the process is smooth.

### With Getcho:

-

Smart targeting : Only customers within 80 miles of a Highline Commerce fulfillment center - a group of nearly 20 million customers - can see the “same-day delivery” option at checkout

-

Automatic prioritization : When customers make a purchase, Getcho automatically expedites package processing by setting a higher priority score

-

Seamless notifications : Highline uses Getcho’s Slack app which notifies stakeholders including Highline’s packers, account managers, and brand managers

-

Integrated fulfillment : Packers use the same exact fulfillment process for courier deliveries as standard deliveries; Getcho’s Packiyo integration prints a same-day delivery label that can be scanned by a courier, the same way a UPS driver would scan a shipping label

-

Real-time tracking : When Highline’s packers print the label, Getcho provides the customer with a custom-branded tracking page that reflects the courier’s location and a to-the-minute ETA

-

AI-powered coordination : Getcho’s software suite fully coordinates with the courier via AI agents, ensuring every order is delivered

## Key Takeaways

- Highline Commerce is a 3PL with fulfillment centers in Brooklyn and Atlanta, serving high-end brands like Coca-Cola and Delta with same-day courier delivery.

- 92-minute average delivery time — achieved by integrating Getcho with Highline’s Packiyo warehouse management system (WMS).

- Before Getcho , brands had to manually coordinate courier pickups, packages were lost without proof of delivery, and customers got no tracking or branded experience.

- Getcho’s Packiyo integration lets packers use the same fulfillment process for courier deliveries as standard shipping — same label, same scan, different speed.

- Smart targeting ensures only customers within 80 miles of a fulfillment center see “same-day delivery” at Shopify checkout — reaching nearly 20 million potential customers.

- The branded tracking page shows the courier’s live location and a to-the-minute ETA under the brand’s own logo — not Getcho’s.

## FAQ (full answers)

### What is Getcho?

Getcho ("get-cho") is a delivery platform designed for businesses. We simplify local deliveries, pickups, and returns using AI-powered tools to reduce errors, improve reliability, and scale operations—helping businesses meet customer expectations and grow without adding staff.

### How do I get started?

Request a demo at getcho.app. From there, we will set up your business dashboard and integrate your Shopify store or other systems as needed.

### What platforms does Getcho integrate with?

We integrate with Shopify, Shopify POS (including POS Lite via our native POS Extension), RICS Software, Packiyo, CleanCloud, Slack, WhatsApp, and custom APIs. Whatever your business needs, we can build it. Schedule a demo to discuss your specific integration requirements.

### Does Getcho work inside Shopify POS?

Yes. The Getcho Shopify POS Extension embeds the same-day delivery queue directly in Shopify POS — including POS Lite, with no POS Pro subscription required. Your team sees a tabbed task view (Need to Pack, On Pickup, On Dropoff, Delivered), scans items with the POS camera for barcode verification, and dispatches a courier in one tap. Slack or SMS pings when a new order hits the queue.

### How does Getcho's AI help my business?

Our AI manages the complex logistics so you don't have to—from smart fleet matching to automatic issue resolution. We handle all the operational details, allowing you to focus on growing your business.

### How does Getcho scale with my business?

Getcho helps businesses handle high delivery volumes by enabling one manager to oversee many deliveries at once, cutting costs and improving efficiency.

### What scale of deliveries can Getcho handle?

Getcho can handle very large delivery volumes. We've successfully processed over 100 orders in under 2 hours for clients. Our AI-powered platform scales to meet your business needs, whether you're doing 10 deliveries a day or 1,000+.

### What types of businesses use Getcho?

Getcho is trusted by a wide range of businesses, including wineries managing direct-to-consumer deliveries, high-end produce and specialty food businesses, stores supporting store-to-store or warehouse-to-store transfers, high-end retailers offering same-day or scheduled deliveries, clothing boutiques, florists and gift shops, rental businesses managing drop-offs and pickups, and SMBs looking to scale logistics without increasing headcount.

### What kind of analytics does Getcho provide?

We provide comprehensive analytics including cart conversion data, customer sentiment analysis, and detailed delivery metrics. These insights help you optimize your delivery operations and improve customer satisfaction.

### How much does a delivery cost?

Pricing is flexible based on your business needs. We offer subscription plans, per-delivery pricing, and custom pricing for larger volumes. Contact us for more details.

### Does Getcho offer white-label delivery tracking?

Yes, you can custom-brand all tracking experiences to match your business. Your customers get a consistent, branded experience regardless of which fleet delivers their order. Branding is optional and fully configurable.

### Can I manage multiple locations with Getcho?

Yes, Getcho supports multi-location businesses by centralizing delivery management, enabling seamless coordination between stores, warehouses, and customers.

### Can I customize delivery zones and hours?

Yes, you can configure custom delivery zones by zip code or radius from your store locations. You can also set specific delivery hours and days to match your business operations.

### Does Getcho support custom integrations?

Yes, we can build custom integrations to meet your business needs. As developers at heart, we're ready to create tailored solutions—just reach out to request custom integrations.

### Does Getcho support bulk order uploads?

Yes, we allow bulk order imports to streamline large-scale delivery scheduling and processing.

### What areas does Getcho service?

Getcho delivers nationwide across the United States. Whether you are in a major metro area or a smaller market, our multi-fleet network provides coverage wherever your customers are.

### What can my business send with Getcho?

Businesses use Getcho to deliver items like retail orders, returns, rental equipment, and more. We support everything from sedans for a few items to box trucks with lift gates—our AI finds the best fleet for each delivery. Contact us if you have special delivery requirements.

### Can Getcho handle time-sensitive or perishable deliveries?

Yes. Short transit times are the best protection for perishable items — same-day local delivery means your products spend minutes in transit, not days. Pair that with your own packaging and Getcho handles the rest. Contact us to discuss your specific requirements.

### Can I track my delivery?

Yes, all deliveries include real-time tracking, audit logs, and proof-of-delivery photos to ensure transparency and reliability. Premium plans offer a custom tracking link and allow multiple recipients to receive updates and notifications on orders.

### What types of notifications do my customers receive?

Customers receive real-time updates via SMS or email, including order confirmations, delivery tracking, and proof-of-delivery notifications.

### What insurance options are available?

Insurance coverage is available for your deliveries. Options range from standard coverage to custom policies for higher-value items based on your average cargo value. Contact us to discuss the right coverage for your business.

### What happens if a delivery goes wrong?

We use AI-powered follow-ups to resolve issues quickly, reducing claims and improving customer satisfaction. In cases where issues cannot be resolved immediately, insurance coverage options are available to protect your shipments.

### Can Getcho handle returns?

Yes, Getcho supports local returns, including same-day return pickups. We also offer a Shopify integration that streamlines the return process for both regular purchases and rental items.

### Does Getcho support rentals?

Yes, we support businesses offering rentals by managing deliveries and pickups for rental items. Customers can schedule flexible delivery and return times to meet their needs.

### Does Getcho support round trips?

Yes. Getcho supports same-day round trips, where a single driver completes the delivery and returns to your store on the same run — bringing back signed paperwork, reusable totes and containers, or equipment. A driver can also make a stop and come back to where they started, all in one dispatched job.

### Can Getcho handle recurring deliveries?

Yes, we support recurring and subscription-based deliveries. We save customer profiles and delivery preferences, so the experience is consistent—customers don't have to repeat their instructions with each delivery.

### Can I schedule a delivery in advance?

Yes, deliveries can be scheduled up to 7 days in advance, ensuring flexibility and convenience.

### How quickly can Getcho deliver a package?

Deliveries are typically dispatched within minutes. Multi-signal dispatch sends your order to multiple fleets simultaneously — the first available driver wins. Most orders are completed within hours.

### How will I know if something goes wrong with a pickup — like a driver grabbing the wrong order?

You'll be notified, fast. Getcho actively monitors every delivery and surfaces issues like a mismatched or missed pickup so your team can send a replacement right away. You choose how you hear about it — Slack, SMS, or email — and notifications are fully configurable. For most stores we also recommend barcode verification at pickup, which scans each item against the order so the wrong package is caught before it ever leaves the door. And when it's a no-harm mix-up (a driver marks picked up without actually grabbing the order, or returns unnecessarily), Getcho will often redispatch on the store's behalf automatically — frequently before anyone has to lift a finger. We stay very hands-on with our store teams.

### What happens after I send an order to Getcho via API, and how fast is it assigned to a driver?

For all intents and purposes, immediately. Once a quote is accepted, the order enters dispatch. Our most common workflow assigns the cheapest available carrier, and in that case the order is assigned to a delivery partner right away. If speed is what you care about most, we can optimize for the fastest available driver instead — dispatch is modular, so we're happy to chat about what fits your operation. For orders scheduled in advance, the same applies as the delivery window approaches, and scheduled orders can be canceled for free up until dispatch.

### Can I update an order after it has been sent to Getcho but before a driver is assigned?

Yes — this happens all the time, and we use APIs to update orders on the fly. Before a driver is assigned, order details can be modified directly. Even after a driver has picked up, reach out and we can usually still get updated instructions where they need to go.

### If a driver is already assigned and I need to cancel because the order isn't ready, how does that work — and who covers the cost?

It depends on timing. If a driver is already en route, the fleet usually charges a cancellation fee, which is passed along. If the cancellation was due to a Getcho dispatch mistake, Getcho may absorb that fee. And if "not ready yet" is something your store runs into regularly, let's talk — we've got solutions, including dispatching only once an order is actually packed rather than purely around the scheduled window.

# Case Study: Release Valves, Reach, and Rates: Supplementing Local Delivery with Getcho | Getcho

**URL:** [https://getcho.app/success-story/supplementing-local-delivery-with-getcho/](https://getcho.app/success-story/supplementing-local-delivery-with-getcho/)

>

Getcho has been extremely helpful in expanding our range of delivery options. And, since we started using Getcho about two months ago, there has been a significant drop in customer experience issues related to third-party delivery. The Getcho team is hands-on and highly responsive to feedback.

— Director of Systems, Farm Link Hawai’i

O’ahu residents island-wide know and love Farm Link Hawaii ’s delivery trucks. You might see them on any given day from Honolulu to Pearl City.

Customers place orders on Farm Link Hawaii’s Shopify website. Before, customers could choose delivery for the next day or later. With Getcho, Farm Link Hawaii launched same-day delivery. And for certain zip codes, Farm Link supplements their next-day vehicles with Getcho.

New York City’s “Color Authority,” Janovic , also runs their own trucks. Janovic supplies builders and painters throughout the boroughs.

## The Challenge

Businesses running their own vehicles know how challenging logistics can be. At volume, it’s nearly impossible to design the perfect route. That’s before throwing in a few more variables:

- Customer receiving hours. Some buildings are closed for deliveries at certain times

- Time in transit. How long can the cargo sit in the truck?

- Audibles, cancellations, and returns

- Traffic variability based on timing

Next-day delivery was once the standard—and many customers still plan their orders in advance. But estimates are just that: jobs change, people forget things, tools break. Janovic and Farm Link Hawaii alike—about as different as two businesses can be—know it’s essential to support urgent cases. Customers will gladly pay a premium, and it keeps them coming back for more typical next-day deliveries.

Carefully planned routes don’t play nicely with urgent delivery. Trucks are already loaded a certain way. Every stop adds incremental uncertainty to all the ones that follow (fact: if you’re stop #16, your reliable delivery window can be as wide as 3–4 hours).

## The Solution

Getcho is the release valve that allows Janovic and Farm Link Hawaii to be meticulous about their next-day routes, while still saying “yes, of course” to the customer who wants to pay extra to receive their delivery in a few hours.

Partners simply enter their urgent deliveries into the Getcho dispatch platform. Getcho runs rates and time windows across a few dozen providers like Roadie, Uber Direct, Bungii, and more. Getcho books mopeds, 53-footers, and everything in between. And we handle keeping both customers and ops teams up to date—knowing with full confidence that everything will be delivered.

### Reaching new markets

Ideally, every new customer sits right along an existing route. Each new customer adds only a marginal delivery cost—right?

Unfortunately, it usually doesn’t work that way. Adding new postal codes can mean hiring another driver, which means absorbing large fixed costs until the route reaches scale.

With Getcho, businesses can support new markets without massively increasing costs. Since we work with so many delivery service providers, we offer broad coverage and pricing that’s proportional to distance and order size—not the cost of adding a new truck.

Farm Link Hawaii and Janovic both use Getcho specifically for zip codes that don’t fall along their existing routes. With Getcho, offering an expansive delivery range is as easy as drawing a circle on a map.

## The Results

That’s why we hear things like:

- “I enjoyed the first-rate customer experience. I will be ordering more from you.” (Farm Link Hawaii customer)

- “My delivery was very smooth and it came much earlier than I expected. I’ll take time writing a review tonight. Thank you again for the fantastic service.” (Eataly customer)

---

Farm Link Hawaii and Janovic use Getcho to supplement their in-house fleets, handle urgent deliveries, and expand into new markets—without adding trucks or complexity.

Book a demo and see how we can help with same-day and next-day delivery.

## Key Takeaways

- Getcho acts as a “release valve” for businesses with their own delivery trucks — handling urgent same-day orders that don’t fit into planned next-day routes.

- Farm Link Hawaii uses Getcho to supplement their island-wide delivery trucks with same-day delivery and to cover zip codes outside their existing routes.

- Janovic (NYC paint supplier) uses Getcho for urgent builder and painter deliveries that can’t wait for the next planned truck route.

- Adding new postal codes with your own fleet means hiring another driver and absorbing fixed costs until the route scales. With Getcho, you pay proportional to distance and order size — no new trucks needed.

- Carefully planned next-day routes break when you inject urgent deliveries: every added stop creates uncertainty for all stops that follow. Keeping urgent orders on Getcho preserves route reliability.

- Customers gladly pay a premium for urgent same-day delivery, and the option keeps them coming back for regular next-day orders too.

## Four steps from install to first delivery

Install From the Shopify App Store Find Getcho in the Shopify App Store and install with one click. The app connects to your store immediately — no API keys, no developer, no lengthy setup process.

Configure Delivery Zones and Cutoff Times Set your delivery radius by zip code or distance, define preparation and cutoff times, configure store hours, and choose which products are eligible. Block specific dates or set holiday schedules.

Customers See Same-Day Delivery at Checkout When a customer checks out near a location with inventory, they see a same-day delivery option with dynamic pricing based on distance. The delivery window respects your cutoff times and store hours.

Mark Fulfilled — Driver Auto-Dispatched When you mark an order as fulfilled in Shopify, Getcho automatically dispatches a driver matched by vehicle size, timing, and distance. Tracking is added to the Shopify order. No phone calls, no copy-pasting.

Can I use Getcho with Shopify POS? Yes. Getcho ships a dedicated Shopify POS Extension that embeds the same-day delivery queue directly inside Shopify POS. Your store team sees every order that needs packing today across tabs — Need to Pack, On Pickup, On Dropoff, Delivered — and can dispatch a courier in one tap without leaving POS. Works on Shopify POS Lite — no POS Pro subscription required.
Does the Shopify POS Extension require POS Pro? No. The Getcho POS Extension works on Shopify POS Lite, which is included with every Shopify plan. Single-location stores, bakeries, florists, and wine shops can run same-day delivery operations from the register without upgrading to POS Pro.
How does barcode verification work in Shopify POS? The Getcho POS Extension uses the device camera to scan barcodes as your team packs each order. Scanning confirms the right SKU is going in the bag. For items without barcodes — fresh goods, custom orders, florals, wine — the team uses a checklist fallback and taps each row as packed. Nothing ships unverified.
How do store teams get notified of new same-day orders? When a same-day order comes in, the Getcho POS Extension pings your team via Slack or SMS — whichever channel you configure. The order appears automatically in the Need to Pack tab inside Shopify POS, so whoever is on the floor can pick it up without checking a separate tablet in the back.
How does multi-location routing work with Shopify? Getcho reads your Shopify locations and inventory levels. When an order comes in, it identifies the nearest store with available stock and routes the delivery from that location. This reduces delivery time and cost automatically.
What delivery options do my customers see at checkout? Customers near a location with inventory see a same-day delivery option at checkout with dynamic pricing based on distance. You control which products are eligible, the delivery radius, cutoff times, and the delivery window displayed.
Can Getcho handle returns and rental pickups through Shopify? Yes. Schedule same-day return pickups and rental item returns directly from your Shopify admin. Drivers pick up from the customer and deliver back to your store or warehouse with full tracking and proof of delivery.
Does Getcho support inventory transfers between Shopify locations? Yes. Use the same courier network to move stock between your Shopify locations same-day. Warehouse to store, store to store — with real-time tracking and proof of delivery at every step.
How much does the Shopify integration cost? Getcho offers a free plan to get started. Pricing is flexible based on delivery volume — we offer per-delivery pricing, subscription plans, and custom enterprise pricing. Install the app from the Shopify App Store to see current plans.

Out-of-stock at fulfillment shouldn't kill the order. Getcho swaps unavailable SKUs for comparable items via Shopify's order-edit API — your customer still gets their order, your record stays clean.

How It Works

## The order keeps moving when stock runs out

Out-of-stock at fulfillment is one of the most expensive moments in DTC — cancellations kill the order, partial fulfillment frustrates the customer, and refund flows tie up your team. Item substitution turns that moment into a simple swap.

Triggered at fulfillment Substitution fires when picking or inventory check discovers a SKU isn't actually on the shelf. The cart-stage flow is unaffected — substitution only kicks in once you're about to fulfill.

Native Shopify order-edit Substitution uses Shopify's order-edit API, so the customer's order record stays accurate. No manual cancellation, no separate replacement order, no reconciliation headache.

Configurable substitution rules You define what swaps for what — a specific SKU pair, a tier within a collection, or fallbacks across multiple alternatives. The fulfillment side picks the right replacement based on your rules.

Customer notification Configure how (or whether) the customer is notified about the swap. Some merchants want a heads-up email, others want it silent if the swap is comparable. You decide.

Pairs with inventory confirmation Getcho's inventory confirmation flow verifies stock before fulfillment leaves. If a SKU isn't there, item substitution applies automatically based on your rules — instead of dead-ending the order.

Shopify-only capability Item substitution at fulfillment is currently Shopify-only because it relies on Shopify's order-edit API. Other platforms are not supported today.
Request a Demo

Item Substitution FAQ

## Common questions about Shopify item substitution

Can't find what you're looking for? Reach out to us .
What is item substitution on Shopify? Item substitution is a Getcho capability for Shopify merchants that swaps an out-of-stock SKU for a comparable item at the fulfillment step — instead of cancelling or partially fulfilling the order. The swap is applied via Shopify's order-edit API so the order record stays accurate.
When does substitution happen? At fulfillment — when the picking team or inventory check discovers a SKU isn't actually available. Rather than cancel the line, Getcho applies the configured substitute, edits the Shopify order, and the delivery proceeds.
Is substitution available outside Shopify? Item substitution at fulfillment is currently a Shopify-only capability because it relies on Shopify's order-edit API. Other platforms are not supported today.
Does the customer know an item was swapped? Yes. The Shopify order is edited so the customer's order record reflects what they actually received, and you can configure customer notifications to communicate the swap.
How is the substitute SKU chosen? You configure substitution rules — what swaps for what — as part of your Shopify catalog setup with Getcho. Talk to our team to scope the right substitution rules for your inventory.
Does substitution affect the original payment? Substitution uses Shopify's native order-edit flow, which handles any pricing differences according to your store's Shopify configuration. Refunds, charges, or no-change scenarios all flow through Shopify the same way they would for any other order edit.
How does this work with the inventory confirmation flow? Getcho's inventory confirmation flow verifies stock at the picking store before fulfillment leaves. If stock isn't there, item substitution can apply automatically based on your configured rules — keeping the order moving instead of dead-ending it.

### What is item substitution on Shopify?

Item substitution is a Getcho capability for Shopify merchants that swaps an out-of-stock SKU for a comparable item at the fulfillment step — instead of cancelling or partially fulfilling the order. The swap is applied via Shopify's order-edit API so the order record stays accurate.

### When does substitution happen?

At fulfillment — when the picking team or inventory check discovers a SKU isn't actually available. Rather than cancel the line, Getcho applies the configured substitute, edits the Shopify order, and the delivery proceeds.

### Is substitution available outside Shopify?

Item substitution at fulfillment is currently a Shopify-only capability because it relies on Shopify's order-edit API. Other platforms are not supported today.

### Does the customer know an item was swapped?

Yes. The Shopify order is edited so the customer's order record reflects what they actually received, and you can configure customer notifications to communicate the swap.

### How is the substitute SKU chosen?

You configure substitution rules — what swaps for what — as part of your Shopify catalog setup with Getcho. Talk to our team to scope the right substitution rules for your inventory.

### Does substitution affect the original payment?

Substitution uses Shopify's native order-edit flow, which handles any pricing differences according to your store's Shopify configuration. Refunds, charges, or no-change scenarios all flow through Shopify the same way they would for any other order edit.

### How does this work with the inventory confirmation flow?

Getcho's inventory confirmation flow verifies stock at the picking store before fulfillment leaves. If stock isn't there, item substitution can apply automatically based on your configured rules — keeping the order moving instead of dead-ending it.
